structured_output.conclusion: None of the three offers can be supported on the current evidence. Knight's senior secured loan terms say Synergy shall not add any other debt without paying Knight out first (fnd_009). A default on any third-party debt automatically defaults the Knight loan (fnd_010), and a Knight default also defaults the Sanders loan (fnd_030). Any of the three advances therefore depends on Knight's consent, which the evidence does not show. That consent is the pivotal missing fact. Second, $2.6M of 2024 settlement payments remain ($2.0M Atrium, $0.6M supplier). Against ~$2.0M reported cash and the illustrative $200k reserve, Synergy is short $800k–$900k if nothing has been paid since June 30, 2024, $150k–$250k if 25% has been paid, and $0 if half or more has been paid (eff_002, eff_005, sensitivity run). Shopify debt must also be paid off by December 31, 2024 (eff_013). If Knight's consent is documented and most of the 2024 settlement payments are shown paid, the offers can then be compared on operating receipts. Otherwise the requested advance cannot be supported. The link between the VitBest row and the March 2024 supplier settlement is an inference from matching amounts. No lending action was taken. The packet is locked but not complete: 15 inventory items (debt, legal, covenant, cash-restriction and accounting) were escalated and remain open for the reviewer.
